assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction broke the long-standing resolution limit set by spherical aberration of round electron lenses and opened atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy of materials, interfaces and defects. This is a genuine invention, experimentally demonstrated, and it changed an entire instrument class used across physics, chemistry and materials science. It is the kind of new tool that opens a door to phenomena that could not be seen before.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector, Haider led the realization of the hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban led the demonstration in the Julich group of sub-angstrom imaging. The supplied names support a clean three-person configuration. Other contributors to aberration-corrected STEM (for example Krivanek and Dellby, who are not credited on this ballot entry) may raise allocation questions that I cannot resolve from the text supplied.
assessment.maturity: Correctors have been commercial for roughly two decades and results are reproduced in many independent laboratories worldwide, so confirmation is overwhelming. Recognition is, if anything, overdue. I am a microscopist and a colleague of these communities, so I note that my enthusiasm should be weighed against possible subject-area bias.
uncertainties: Priority and credit between the TEM and STEM correction efforts is not fully settled from the supplied text.
Whether the committee regards this as physics rather than instrumentation for materials science is a framing risk.
My own field proximity could bias the assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos (2013) with a cubic-kilometre Antarctic detector opened neutrino astronomy and was followed by the first evidence of a neutrino source (TXS 0506+056, 2017-2018). It is an experimental discovery of a new messenger and an instrument that opens a door onto the high-energy universe.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept and its science case; Karle was a leading experimental figure in the detector construction and early results. Spiering is a credible alternative for early work (DUMAND and Baikal lineage), but a two-person configuration with Halzen and Karle seems most defensible from the supplied names. The large collaboration makes any individual attribution delicate.
assessment.maturity: The astrophysical flux has been independently confirmed with multiple channels and by other detectors in recent years. Source identification is still limited, but the original discovery is secure and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Origin of the neutrinos is only partly identified, which may make the interpretive side premature.
Attribution within a roughly 300-member collaboration and across the DUMAND, Baikal and AMANDA predecessors is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states opened the field of moire quantum matter, with a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. It is original, experimentally verified and very influential.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction (2011) and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery (2018). The supplied names map naturally to a theory plus experiment configuration of three. Cory Dean, Kim and others on related moire work are not credited here and may be claimed by others.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the superconducting and correlated states and the field is rapidly extended to other moire systems. The mechanism of superconductivity remains debated, so the interpretation is not entirely stable, but the experimental discovery itself is robust.
uncertainties: Sample-dependent behaviour and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility.
Other groups' experimental contributions may complicate credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength proposal and its realization in strontium, delivered fractional uncertainty at the 10^-18 level and is poised to redefine the second and enable tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. It is an invention with demonstrated performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks, and Ye realized the record-performing strontium clocks. This two-person credit is plausible, though ion clocks, and the 2005 frequency-comb prize, make allocation of credit for the clock family sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks around the world agree at extreme precision, so confirmation is strong. Redefinition of the second is expected but not yet done, so some may consider the societal impact still upcoming.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior recognition of optical frequency combs and atomic clock work.
Redefinition of the SI second is still pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, established a new class of topological electronic phases. The idea is original, experimentally verified and widely influential in materials and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp led the experimental discovery in HgTe wells in 2007 following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not credited here, so credit allocation is a real issue. The supplied three names are a coherent configuration though contested by Zhang's group's claims.
assessment.maturity: The spin Hall edge transport has been repeated and extended to 3D topological insulators in several materials by independent groups. Interpretation is stable. Applications remain limited, though the understanding contribution is clear.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's prediction for HgTe is outside the credited names, which complicates attribution.
Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phases of matter may reduce the novelty in the committee's eyes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave resonators and underpins readout and control in today's superconducting quantum processors. The original experiment was a clear demonstration with lasting impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the theoretical proposal (2004) and Wallraff and Schoelkopf realized the strong-coupling experiments in the same year. A three-person theory plus experiment configuration is workable; Yale colleagues such as Devoret are not named here, and Devoret was recognized in 2025 for a related circuit work.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and adopted widely, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits reduces the near-term appetite for another superconducting-circuit prize.
uncertainties: Recent recognition of a closely related field may make this premature or redundant.
Allocation among the Yale, Saclay and Delft pioneers is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of quantized conductance in ballistic point contacts (1988) was a simple, clean and original experiment that revealed conductance quantization in units of 2e^2/h and became a foundation of mesoscopic physics and quantum devices. It is precisely the original experiment, even if not elaborate.
assessment.attribution: The 1988 discoveries were made independently by the Delft/Philips group (van Wees and colleagues) and by the Cambridge group (Wharam, Pepper and colleagues). Naming van Wees and Pepper is plausible, but it omits co-authors such as Thornton, Wharam and Ritchie, and the prize rule of three may force hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed over more than three decades and incorporated into textbooks, so there is no maturity concern, though the very long delay raises the question of whether the window has passed.
uncertainties: Joint discovery by two groups and several co-authors makes the allocation delicate.
Possible view that the effect is a foundational but now routine component.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state quantum system used for nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and quantum information. It is a new tool that lets us measure things that could not be measured before, including in biological contexts.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated the single-centre optical detection and spin control (1997 onward); Lukin's group played a large role in sensing and quantum register demonstrations, though Lukin's contributions are arguably broader than this topic. Other groups such as Awschalom and Hanson also contributed to coherent spin control and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in many laboratories and increasingly commercial, but applications are still maturing, so some consider it somewhat early.
uncertainties: Credit from others (Awschalom, Hanson, Walsworth, Yacoby) may be underrepresented.
Which part of the NV work, discovery or application, is the prizeworthy core is unclear.
